analysis.title: The tech puke is done
key_insights: The Market Ear asks whether the tech selloff has run its course. Hedge fund tech exposure is at historic lows and the momentum trade has been dismantled, while AI spending continues, earnings expectations are resetting and a first bounce has started.
Goldman's prime book shows the US technology long/short ratio at 1.5, down from 2.14 in June. That is the lowest reading since the series began in 2016.

BofA's survey shows the net % overweight in Tech fell to roughly -27 ppt, one of the steepest monthly declines in the series and comparable to the 2004 washout. 52% of respondents now expect AI hyperscaler capex cuts.
Global hedge fund net exposure has flipped slightly negative as equity long/short funds and multi-strats abandon the momentum factor. Only quants remain net long, and they are well below their highs.
JPM PI data shows institutional exposure to AI-related equities at its lowest level since April 2025.
Vanda and Sober Look note a first bounce and a potential double bottom forming. Positioning is washed out, and the lows now need to hold.
Bloomberg data shows NDX back near its long-term trendline. The short-term picture is weak, but the long-term trend is still intact.

Goldman sees roughly 40% upside to Nvidia in its base case and 175% in its bull case. Nvidia says it intends to return all excess cash to shareholders, with about $227 billion of buyback authorization remaining.
Goldman expects AI infrastructure earnings growth to slow from nearly 90% to below 20% by 2029. The Market Ear reads the reset in expectations as a possible setup for upside surprises.
Morgan Stanley Research sees hyperscaler capex rising from $951 billion in 2026 to more than $1.6 trillion in 2027 and almost $1.8 trillion in 2028. Growth is slowing from very high levels.

More than half of Nasdaq 100 constituents are in bear-market territory. Sentiment Trader data shows that when the 10-day average crosses above 51.5%, the Nasdaq has gained an average of 5% over the next three months, with positive returns 59% of the time.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is washed out, a first bounce and potential double bottom have formed, hyperscaler capex keeps rising per Morgan Stanley, and Sentiment Trader data shows an average 5% three-month gain after similar breadth readings.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman expects AI infrastructure earnings growth to slow from nearly 90% to below 20% by 2029, 52% of BofA respondents expect capex cuts, and the short-term NDX picture is weak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The recent lows need to hold. A break below them would invalidate the double-bottom case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Positioning is washed out and the first bounce is in, so the bulls have something to work with if the lows hold.
